history.period: 1128-1500 CE (rebuilds and additions; pilgrimage tradition far older)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. The Girnar Jain temples are a group of Svetambara Jain temples plus one Digambara temple atop Mount Girnar near Junagadh, sacred because the 22nd Tirthankara Neminath attained omniscience and moksha here; some 16 sculpted temples form a fort-like cluster on a cliff ledge. The principal Neminath temple, a black-grey granite shrine, was rebuilt c. 1128-1159 CE by Sajjana, governor of Saurashtra under Solanki king Jayasimha Siddharaja; a Mallinath temple was erected in 1177, and further temples date to 1230-1500 CE, with a 17th-century outer hall and a 1364 CE gilding by Chudasama king Mandalika I. NOTE: Wikipedia's Girnar article records a disputed claim that the Neminath shrine on the highest peak was converted into the Dattatreya Hindu temple (see seq 291, Dattatreya Temple); the conversion allegation is contested. Coordinates used are for the main Neminath temple cluster (21.5264, 70.5234), corroborated by a business listing for 'Jain temple Neminath Bhagwan Girnar' (21.526401, 70.523419).

name: Girnar Jain Temples
town_description: Junagadh is a historic city in Gujarat's Saurashtra region, nestled at the foot of Mount Girnar. Its past stretches from Ashoka's 3rd-century BCE rock edicts and the Uparkot Fort to the Nawabi-era Mahabat Maqbara, and it is a major pilgrimage hub for both Hindus and Jains.

travel.airport: Keshod (~40 km) or Rajkot (~103 km) from Junagadh
travel.railway: Junagadh Junction (~6 km from Girnar Taleti, the base)
travel.road: Girnar Taleti base is reached by road from Junagadh; the temple cluster is then a climb of ~4,000-5,000 steps; ropeway runs to Ambaji temple nearby

visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx. 5 AM-8 PM (one listing shows these hours; the larger Neminath temple is reported open through midday unlike smaller shrines)
